title: Autoguided Admin Shell + Runbook-as-Data Curator (vectorized guidance & safe-exec)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build an "autoguided" admin shell that surfaces runbook-as-data suggestions in context, prioritized by recent incident telemetry and by similarity to the current debugging context. The feature consists of two main parts: (1) a Runbook Curator service that converts canonical runbooks (YAML/MD/action-steps) into vectorized, searchable fragments with metadata (preconditions, safe-mode tags, RBAC limits, cost estimates), and (2) an Autoguided Shell UX that retrieves ranked suggestions, shows quick-read verification (diff / dry-run), and provides a one-click safe-exec flow with auditable approval and optional canary execution on a staging agent before production commands run.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to remediation (MTTR) for common platform incidents by 30% for P1/P2 operational flows.
- Encourage runbooks-as-code: treat runbooks as first-class retrievable artifacts, enable incremental updates, and automatically surface the most-relevant remediation step for the active context.
- Protect production by enforcing safety policies (RBAC, read-only fallbacks, dry-run gating, mandatory review for high-risk commands).

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full incident playbook automation or autopilot remediations in this phase. This work focuses on guided human-in-the-loop UX, not fully autonomous corrective agents.

Design overview:
1) Runbook Curator
   - Ingest existing runbooks from the runbook-repo and Confluence exports (YAML, markdown).
   - Normalize into step-level fragments with metadata fields: intent, preconditions, side-effects, estimated token/cost, risk-level.
   - Generate dense embeddings (vector store) via the internal Redwood embedding pipeline; store sparse metadata in Postgres and vectors in the vector DB.
   - Periodically re-run vectorization after runbook edits and automatically tag steps with recent telemetry signals (last 90d execution frequency, success rate).

2) Autoguided Shell (affordances)
   - Context collector: capture CLI/context signals (service, region, user role, recent traces/err IDs) and synthesize a short retrieval query.
   - Retriever + re-ranker: query vector store -> candidate steps -> re-rank by telemetry relevance and RBAC compatibility.
   - UI flow: show 3 candidate steps with short rationale, risk indicators, required approvals, and a dry-run toggle.
   - Safe-exec flow: if step is low-risk and within user’s RBAC, allow one-click exec; else route to a staged approval channel (Slack / Console approvals). All executions emit structured audit logs and tokenized diffs for replay.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end demo: ingest 10 representative runbooks, produce vector index, and show retrievals for 5 synthetic incident contexts.
- Telemetry integration: retrieval ranking must use at least one telemetry signal (execution frequency or success rate).
- Safety checks: at least three command-level policies enforced (RBAC, dry-run enforcement for high-risk, approval required for fatal-side-effect steps).
- Performance: retrieval+re-rank latency under 250ms for 95th percentile in the staging environment.
- Tests: unit tests for curator parsers, integration test for retrieval pipeline, and an e2e smoke demonstrating safe-exec audit entry in the event log.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Precompute vs. on-the-fly embeddings: precomputing reduces runtime latency but increases storage and requires reindexing on edits. We chose precompute for retrieval latency goals and will implement incremental reindexing hooks on git-webhook updates.
- Vector store selection: initial PoC uses the in-house vector index for access control hooks; future work may migrate to managed DB if scale/ops cost dictates.
- Safety model: conservative-by-default (deny exec unless explicitly allowed). This reduces friction for common cases; we'll add opt-in 'accelerated mode' for trusted SRE groups later.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: stale runbooks leading to bad suggestions. Mitigation: show last-updated timestamp + telemetry freshness and add a 'verify on staging' badge.
- Risk: leaking internal secrets in step fragments. Mitigation: curator redacts secrets, and embeddings are generated from sanitized text; security review required.
- Risk: vector-index drift causing noisy retrievals. Mitigation: periodic re-index job and an evaluation harness (see links).

Telemetry & success metrics:
- MTTR reduction measured on sampled P1 incidents where curated suggestions were used.
- Time-to-first-suggestion (target < 5s for UI open).
- False-positive rate: percent of suggested steps that were not applicable (target < 20% after two weeks of usage).

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Curator ingestion job (parser + normalizer + embedding pipeline).
- Retriever + re-ranker service and a small public API.
- Autoguided Shell prototype integrated into the operator console and as a local CLI shim.
- Security review artifacts and a draft runbook sanitization policy.

Notes on rollout:
- Phase 1 (PoC): internal SRE only, 10 runbooks, read-only suggestions + dry-run for execs.
- Phase 2: expand to broader SRE, enable safe-exec, add approval routing to Console.
- Phase 3: integrate canary executors and automatic remediation bundles (separate initiative).
